A reusable headless Laravel library should make behavior explicit at its seams: typed metadata rather than hidden conventions, database-enforced concurrency and uniqueness, durable intent before external effects, and a constrained query DSL rather than arbitrary client SQL. The matrix below deliberately avoids prescribing any particular product schema.

## Evidence matrix


## Two distinctions that matter


## At-most-one vs exactly-one default

- At-most-one default means the database invariant permits zero or one row marked/default for a scope. It is the right default when a scope can legitimately have no configured default—for example, a newly created workspace.
- Exactly-one default is stronger: every applicable scope must always have one default. A unique/partial unique index alone generally proves only “no more than one”; it does not create a row or prove one exists.
- Enforce exactly-one through a lifecycle protocol: create the default atomically with the scope, serialize reassignment, and prohibit deletion/unsetting of the last default (or use a required pointer from the scope to its selected row). Validate it at the database boundary where feasible, not merely in application code.
- PostgreSQL’s default behavior makes NULL values distinct in unique indexes; choose NULLS NOT DISTINCT, separate partial unique indexes per scope class, or another explicit modeling strategy depending on the portability and version constraints of the library.

## afterCommit vs durable outbox

afterCommit prevents a Laravel queue job/listener from being dispatched before the current database transaction commits. That closes the “worker observed uncommitted state” problem, and discarded rollbacks do not emit the deferred event. It does not, by itself, guarantee recoverable intent across the commit-to-dispatch process boundary.
A durable transactional outbox writes the business mutation and a pending external-effect record to the same database transaction. After commit, independently restartable workers can find, claim, retry, audit, and reconcile that durable intent. It improves atomicity of “state changed + work must eventually be attempted,” but still does not make a non-transactional email/SMS/webhook provider exactly-once; stable delivery keys and explicit unknown outcomes remain necessary.
